summary: YARIN is a localized Martian survival and vital health ecosystem designed to protect astronauts operating outside the habitat where standard GPS and internet infrastructure do not exist. Centered around a robust smartband powered by an ESP32 microcontroller, MAX30102 pulse/oxygen sensor, BMP280 barometer, and MPU6050 kinetic tracker, YARIN maintains a continuous localized safety tether using a LoRa network. It enforces a strict 100-meter safety boundary via RSSI signal tracking without relying on vulnerable satellites. If an astronaut exceeds the safe zone, suffers hypoxia, experiences a sudden fall, or triggers the physical SOS button, an immediate 3-way hardware alarm (buzzer, haptic vibration, and LED flashing) alerts both the astronaut and the rover dashboard. Furthermore, YARIN integrates multi-layered environmental mapping and NASA/JPL-Caltech Mars raw image data to provide pre-arrival terrain awareness, ensuring that surviving on Mars is matched with getting back safely.
details:
YARIN solves the total absence of GPS and cellular communication on Mars by establishing a 100% offline, localized safety ecosystem bridging an astronaut's smartband, a LoRa communication network, and a centralized rover dashboard. It tracks real-time vital signs (SpO2, heart rate), kinetic movements (fall/immobility detection), and proximity to the base using RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) over LoRa.

Hardware Stack:

ESP32: Core processor for logic, Bluetooth, and Wi-Fi bridging.

MAX30102: High-fidelity optical sensor for continuous pulse and SpO2 tracking.

BMP280: Barometric sensor for ambient pressure estimation.

MPU6050: Accelerometer/Gyroscope for motion tracking and fall detection.

LoRa + Alarm Matrix: Offline telemetry with high-decibel buzzer, haptic vibration, and high-intensity LED.

Software & NASA Data Integration: Uses multi-layered environmental awareness (topography, radiation, atmospherics, hydrology, and live astronaut pathing) combined with NASA/JPL-Caltech Mars raw image gallery data, allowing astronauts to preview terrain and landmarks before arrival
